entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Health Canada launches pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials: Notice
entries.description: Health Canada launches a pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials.  If the criteria for the pilot are met and the trial is accepted under the pilot, sponsors will not be expected to comply with all of the regulatory requirements.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched a pilot program for select academic‑led pediatric standard‑of‑care clinical trials that may exempt sponsors from meeting all regulatory requirements if the pilot criteria are met.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams working on pediatric trials must assess whether their studies qualify for the pilot to determine if reduced compliance obligations apply.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register of innovative drugs has been established under sub‑section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor the register to stay aware of which drugs are classified as innovative for compliance and reporting purposes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice for Hernexeos (304237)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada has issued a Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) for Hernexeos, requiring the sponsor to conduct additional studies to verify its clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must prepare for the additional study requirements and monitor compliance with the NOC conditions to maintain market authorization.

entries.summary: CVMP granted a positive opinion for the marketing authorisation of Bovilis Lumpyvax in exceptional circumstances.
entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary product developers should proceed with regulatory submission and marketing activities for this product.

entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: No changes to the NOC database; the release provides data extracts in compressed ASCII format.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams can use the extracts to support compliance reporting and database maintenance.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot that assists sponsors with clinical trial applications will become a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams will now have ongoing access to the ACT EU advisory service, so they should plan for continuous engagement and incorporate its guidance into their application workflows.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: No specific changes identified in the product monograph brand safety updates for submissions cleared between 01‑09‑2026 and 30‑09‑2026.
entries.why_it_matters: No new requirements or implications for RA teams can be derived from the provided information.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance for market authorization holders on how to report and provide information on drug shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams must use this guide to ensure compliance with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations when reporting shortages or discontinuations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance on distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada to help comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Canadian drug establishment license holders must understand the procedures for exporting their products, impacting RA teams involved in regulatory compliance and export planning.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide provides instructions on how drug establishment licence holders can import and sell drugs to address shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must follow the guidance to comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 and ensure uninterrupted access to necessary medicines.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: The guide explains how to extend expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must update product shelf‑life and labeling to comply with the new guidance when shortages occur.

entries.summary: The EMA has issued pre‑authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams involved in centralised procedure submissions should review the guidance to ensure their processes align with EMA expectations.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams will need to incorporate the updated database into their product information workflows to ensure accurate and current data is used for submissions and ongoing compliance.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…

entries.why_it_matters: All RA teams involved in drug development must note that regulatory expectations are shifting toward non‑animal testing methods, requiring review of preclinical data and potential protocol adjustments.
